data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 《Understanding J》是一份简明介绍J编程语言的文档，适合有一定编程经验的读者。J语言源自APL，采用ASCII字符，支持多维数组操作，基本内建函数常为单个符号或附加点、冒号的符号。J中的数据值称为“名词”，包括数字、列表、字符串等，字符串使用单引号且通过双写引号来转义。J还支持一些特殊数据类型，如符号和稀疏数组。文档建议运行示例代码以加深理解，并提供了J语言的在线资源和快速入门指南。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕编程语言J的评价与使用体验，以及对J语言某些特性的疑问和建议

不同观点：
• [vintagedave] 认为J语言在学习过程中非常令人困惑，课程中的编译器/环境存在许多bug，但随着使用更多编程语言，他对J产生了更多兴趣，并希望深入学习。
• [binary132] 提出理想的编程语言应结合 concatenative 语言（如FORTH）和数组编程语言的特点，暗示J在某些方面符合其理想语言的构想。
• [gitroom] 表示J语言中下划线的用法让人困惑，虽然不习惯，但尊重其独特的设计选择。
• [prezjordan] 提供了一个实用建议，建议作者添加一个 .devcontainer 目录和Dockerfile，以便其他人可以通过GitHub Codespaces尝试J语言，并提供了一个示例链接。

补充讨论：
• [preguntador] 对J语言中复数表示法（12j34）的含义提出了疑问，询问这是12j + 34还是12 + 34j，显示出对J语法细节的困惑。
• [t-writescode] 引用了J语言文档中的下划线用法，并对负无穷大和无穷大的表示法提出疑问，显示出对J标准的不熟悉。
• [jbverschoor] 强调J语言与(Visual) J++不同，并称赞了(Visual) J++的IDE，暗示J语言的开发环境可能不如(Visual) J++。
• [userbinator] 以幽默方式猜测标题被截断可能是无意的，暗示对标题不完整的调侃。

争议焦点：
• J语言的独特语法和下划线用法让一些用户感到困惑，如[gitroom]和[t-writescode]所提到的，但也有用户如[jbverschoor]对其独特性表示尊重和欣赏。
• 对J语言中复数表示法和负无穷大表示法的理解存在分歧，显示出用户对J语言某些标准的不熟悉和疑问。

Understanding J
An introduction to the J programming language that gets to the point.
It is intended for those with (some) programming experience, but others
should be mostly fine after looking up some basic programming terms like
function, argument, class, instance, inheritance, statement, expression,
etc.
Don't treat this as a reference: Section titles do not introduce an
exhaustive explanation of a certain topic, but serve to give this
document a rough structure. Individual sections are not intended to be
read in isolation from the others and assume the knowledge of previous
sections.
Run the examples and read the comments!
If you have J installed you can open this file in JQt via the
file-selection dialog which opens with
ctrl+o
(make sure to set the
filetype-filter to "all"). Click on a line with J code and press
ctrl+enter
to execute it.
Covered builtins are listed in the appendix with a short description.
Important links:
Project Homepage:
https://jsoftware.com
Online J interpreter:
https://jsoftware.github.io/j-playground/bin/html2/
All builtin operators
, with links to their wiki pages:
https://code.jsoftware.com/wiki/NuVoc
Good old wiki:
https://www.jsoftware.com/help/dictionary/contents.htm
Cheatsheet/Reference Card (not for beginners):
https://code.jsoftware.com/wiki/File:B.A4.pdf
History:
J was first released in 1990 as a successor to APL, an alternative
mathematical notation that is computer-executable and works well with
multi-dimensional array data. Most notably J switches from APL's custom
symbol-set to ASCII only, calling most basic builtins by a single symbol
or a symbol with appended dot or colon, and giving distinct meaning to
single symbols that usually appear in pairs like various braces and
quotes (
[]"{}
etc).
Comments:
NB.
comments the rest of the line (latin: nota bene).
Numbers:
J has many number-notations; the most important are:

integer
3.14
NB.
float
_3
NB.
negative numbers start with underscore
_
NB.
sole underscore is infinity: a number

NB.
negative infinity
12j34
NB.
complex number (sometimes used as argument pair)
16bcoffee
NB.
base-16 number (must be lowercase)
Lists, Booleans:
The notation is simple: just put elements next to each other. All
elements must to have the same type but as an empty list has no elements
it can be combined with any other list. True and false are represented
simply by the two numbers
1
and
0
. See also: strings
0
1
NB.
the booleans (truth values) in a 2-element list

4
NB.

(

4
)
NB.
error: can't implicitly join lists, see below
Strings:
Strings are lists thus an empty string is commonly used as empty list
notation. The default string type is called "literal" and is UTF-8
encoded which means the first 128 ASCII characters work well with arrays
as they are a single byte long. String literals are singlequoted, and
only this character is special; it is escaped by doubling it. See also:
string representation and unicode
'

NB.
empty string is empty list
'

'
Nouns:
Nouns
are data values such as the ones covered until now.
Boxes
,
which will be covered later, are nouns too. Lists are actually just a
basic case of
arrays
which can be thought of as nested lists.
Classes and their instances aren't nouns: they cannot be referenced
directly; but their name can be saved as a string.
Functions aren't nouns either; but by putting them into a special kind
of list,
gerunds
, they can effectively be made one (also covered
below).
Special data types:
J comes with some specialized data types, which wont be covered here,
but shall at least be mentioned:
Symbols
: They are a specialized type of string, which is
immutable, treated as a single element and has optimized performance
with searching, sorting and comparison operations. However, only a
few, often used ones should be created, as they are registered in a
global table and cannot be removed from it anymore. More info at:
https://code.jsoftware.com/wiki/Vocabulary/sco

data.title: Elvish – Scripting language and interactive shell
data.author: kartikarti
data.article_summary: Elvish 是一个强大的脚本语言和多功能交互式 shell，支持 Linux、BSD、macOS 和 Windows。它尚未发布 1.0 版本，但已足够稳定，可用于脚本编写和交互操作。Elvish 提供详细的用户文档和开发文档，源码采用 BSD-2-Clause 许可，部分代码基于 Go 和 Clojure 等项目，采用不同许可。Elvish 拥有 5.9k 个星标和 311 个分支，由 95 位贡献者开发，主要使用 Go 语言编写。项目网站为 [elv.sh](http://elv.sh)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对Elvish及其他新型shell的看法和使用体验

不同观点：
• [对Elvish的正面评价]  
  - [xiaq] 作为Elvish的作者，提到Elvish每年都会在HN上被讨论，暗示其具有一定的社区关注度。  
  - [atiq-ca] 对Elvish表示兴趣，并询问其是否具有类似Powershell的面向对象功能，表明对这种特性的潜在需求。

• [对Elvish的负面评价和失望]  
  - [Arcuru] 虽然尝试了多种新型shell（oils/ysh, elvish, xonsh），但觉得这些shell引入了一种既不是Python也不是传统shell的语言，增加了学习成本，最终选择fish和Python结合使用，避免使用额外的shell特性。  
  - [photonthug] 认为Elvish的文档写得过于啰嗦，增加了理解难度，尤其是对外部命令的解释让人困惑，甚至怀疑文档是否由AI生成。  
  - [rendaw] 对Elvish非常失望，指出其文档不完整、缺乏后台任务支持、shell钩子有未说明的限制等问题，认为该项目"半生不熟且已停止发展"。

• [对其他shell的偏好]  
  - [gatane] 偏好使用来自Plan9的rc shell，认为它比bash和其他shell更简单，同时提供了必要的功能如函数、for循环和列表。  
  - [linsomniac] 认为zsh已经"足够好"，结合一些插件能提供如fish的优点而没有其缺点，表示没有必要切换到其他新型shell。  
  - [account-5] 喜欢Nushell，因为它改进了bash的一些痛点，并将数据格式作为一等公民，同时指出Elvish在数据解析上的不足。

• [对比与选择困难]  
  - [IshKebab] 认为Elvish比bash好，但市场上还有其他优于bash的选择，需要更多理由来说服用户选择Elvish而非Nushell。  
  - [baobun] 询问是否有用户在日常使用Elvish，希望通过他人经验来判断其价值。

补充讨论：
- Elvish的文档问题是一个争议焦点，部分用户认为其难以理解且过于冗长。
- 不同用户对新型shell的需求和偏好各异，有的追求简单和熟悉（如zsh、rc shell），有的希望有更强大的内置数据处理能力（如Nushell、Powershell）。
- Elvish的开发状态受到质疑，一些用户认为其发展停滞且功能不全。

data.title: Predictions from the METR AI scaling graph are based on a flawed premise
data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于LLM（大型语言模型）能力评估基准的有效性和预测价值

不同观点：
• [hatefulmoron] 认为Y轴应代表模型在循环任务中的实际进展能力，即模型能否在一段时间内自主解决问题。他对当前模型的表现感到失望，并认为自己未仔细查看细节是问题所在。

• [aoeusnth1] 支持当前的基准，认为任务成功率50%的基准是有预测价值的，尽管有人批评任务时长不能完全代表任务难度。他指出，尽管有许多因素影响任务难度，但平均任务时长仍然是衡量难度的好指标。他批评Gary Marcus的观点，认为其忽略了基准的预测能力。

• [yorwba] 建议通过收集不同难度的任务来测试AI的表现，尤其是那些人类表现较好但AI表现较差的任务。这将有助于明确AI当前的局限性，而不是简单地否定所有进展。

• [sandspar] 对Gary Marcus的批评持嘲讽态度，认为其观点过于可预测和重复，建议其不必详细撰写文章，因为结论总是相同。

• [Nivge] 认为基准是基于特定数据集的，虽然不能完全代表AI的整体进展，但仍有其价值和意义。

• [Sharlin] 暗示对某些人未考虑特定软件任务的基准可能不适用于所有认知任务表示不满，似乎对这种局限性并不意外。

• [dist-epoch] 指出某些批评可能基于过时的信息，并提供了一个链接，显示ChatGPT已经通过了某个被认为失败的测试，暗示讨论应基于最新数据。

补充讨论：

data.title: Oberon Pi
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Oberon Pi 是 Richard Gleaves 将 Peter de Wachter 的 Oberon 系统模拟器移植到 Raspberry Pi OS 的版本。Gleaves 是前 UCSD Pascal 项目成员，并撰写了《Modula-2 for Pascal Programmers》一书。Oberon Pi 主要改进了用户界面，简化了新用户的学习曲线，同时保留了 Oberon 系统的核心特性。它还集成了 Andreas Pirklbauer 对 Oberon 编译器的修改，完全实现了 CASE 语句并修复了一些编译器错误。该项目提供了全面的文档和指南，包括新的用户指南和原始 Oberon 文档，并可在 Raspberry Pi 400 上运行。为在 64 位系统上运行，需对设置进行一些调整。所有资源可在 GitHub 上获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"Project Oberon 2013"及其相关技术的讨论，包括其历史、特点、应用以及与其他技术的比较。

不同观点：
• [pdw] 认为 "Project Oberon 2013" 只是一个预装了Oberon模拟器的标准Raspberry Pi Linux发行版。他解释了Oberon的版本历史，指出这个版本代表了Oberon的早期开发阶段，虽然可以构建模拟器，但其功能相对原始。
• [boznz] 分享了个人经验，提到在自己的小说中隐藏了对Wirth和Oberon的隐秘引用，只有少数人能发现这个彩蛋。
• [wirrbel] 指出Oberon和Go语言在结构上的相似性，认为Go语言可能受到了Oberon的启发，并提到了Rob Pike的ACME编辑器。
• [owlstuffing] 推荐了Luca Boasso的oberonc项目，这是一个针对JVM的Oberon项目。
• [skoodge] 提到重读Wirth的《Plea for Lean Software》并认为其观点仍然具有现实意义，同时询问是否有类似Oberon的仍在活跃开发的项目。
• [xkriva11] 提供了另一个基于Ultibo的Oberon版本链接。
• [rbanffy] 提到以前在苹果应用商店上有一个Oberon应用，并提到一个消失的AT&T Blit终端模拟器。
• [teddyh] 对"Raspberry Pi"名称的由来做了有趣的解释，指出其原意是直接启动到Python。
• [lproven] 表示希望看到一个真正的裸机移植版本，并提到A2曾经支持StrongARM裸机。
• [anthk] 提到DuskOS正在整合Oberon。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[qwerty456127] 质疑Oberon的实用性，指出其在Unicode支持、图形支持以及现代网络协议方面的不足。这引发了对Oberon应用场景和局限性的讨论。
• [rbanffy] 提出了一个对比问题，询问学习和使用9front与Oberon之间的区别，这涉及到不同技术选择的学习价值和应用场景。

总的来说，讨论围绕Oberon的历史、技术特点、与其他技术的比较以及其实际应用展开，参与者分享了各自的经验和资源链接。

43885478.article_content:
Oberon, the jewel by Niklaus Wirth and Jürg Gutknecht: Operating System, Compiler and Computer.
Oberon Pi is a port of Peter de Wachter’s Project Oberon emulator to the Raspberry Pi OS by Richard Gleaves.
Richard Gleaves is a former UCSD Pascal Project member, and author of the 1984 Springer book “Modula-2 for Pascal Programmers”.
The software changes were mostly limited to the UI, with the goal of flattening out the learning curve for new users of the Oberon system, not only read about in a few places online, but also experienced firsthand after bringing the system up.
Richard also added
Andreas Pirklbauer
’s changes to the Oberon compiler, to fully implement CASE statements and fix a few compiler bugs.
The main feature in Oberon Pi is its documentation, which includes new user guides Richard wrote for the Oberon operating system and draw application, along with a complete set of Wirth’s original PDF documents on the Oberon language, now made more usable with the addition of TOCs to the PDFs.
Here an uptodate downloadable list of relevant Oberon documents:
Oberon – The Overlooked Jewel, Michael Franz
Compiler Construction, 2017, Niklaus Wirth
Differences between Revised Oberon and Oberon, 2008, Niklaus Wirth
The Programming Language Oberon, 2013/2026
Programming A Tutorial, 1982/2015, Niklaus Wirth
A Plea for Lean Software, Niklaus Wirth
Project Oberon
The Design of an Operating System, a Compiler and a Computer
Revised Edition 2013
Niklaus Wirth, Jurg Gutknecht
Oberon Pi Setup Guide
Oberon Pi Quick Reference
Oberon Pi System User Guide
Oberon Pi Draw Quick Reference
Oberon Pi Draw User Guide
See the github at
https://github.com/richardgleaves/Oberon-Pi
for Oberon Pi, ready to run on the Raspberry Pi OS.
See below how to run Oberon Pi on a 64 bit architecture Raspberry Pi OS.
Oberon Pi
Author
: Richard Gleaves
This version of Oberon, named Oberon Pi, emulates the Oberon system on a Raspberry Pi 400, using the Raspberry Pi OS as the host operating system.
Oberon Pi runs as an application in the Raspberry Pi OS. When you execute the Oberon Pi command, a window opens on the Pi OS desktop. This window is the Oberon *display*, and it works like a separate computer running the Oberon system, with its own windows, command menus, and file system.
Goals
The original Oberon system includes many unusual user interface elements. These elements make the system worthy of study, both as a historical software artifact, and as a case study in user interface design.
But the original system also includes a few non-key features (such as *mouse interclicking* and opaque command names) which make the system difficult to learn.
The primary goal and purpose of Oberon Pi is instructional: to make the original Oberon system more accessible, by updating the non-key user interface elements to contemporary software standards, while preserving the key elements that make Oberon unique.
Oberon Pi includes source code and full documentation of the Oberon system and language. The system user guide is provided as both a standalone PDF file and as integrated help in the Oberon system.
System Requirements
–  Raspberry Pi computer (Pi4 or Pi 5 preferred)
–  32 bit or 64 bit Raspberry Pi OS desktop vrsion(Bookworm or Bullseye)
–  Desktop computer monitor (large preferred)
Installation
For details see the *Oberon Pi Setup Guide*.
History
The Oberon system was originally developed in the late 1980s by Niklaus Wirth and Jürg Gutknecht. In 2013 the system was re-implemented by Wirth and Paul Reed to run on a custom RISC processor. In 2014 an emulator for the RISC processor was developed by Peter De Wachter. Oberon Pi is a port of the emulator to the Raspberry Pi OS.
Install and run on 64 bit Raspberry Pi OS
The github distribution is for the 32 bit Raspberry Pi OS.
Make these changes to run Oberon Pi on a 64 bit Raspberry Pi OS after the initial setup but before launching Oberon Pi:
cd Oberon\Emulator
mv risc risc.pi400
sudo apt install libsdl2-dev
make
which will produce (silently) a new ‘risc’ executable and follow the ‘Oberon Pi Setup Guide’.
Here an archive with both 32 bit and 64 bit ‘risc’ executables.

data.title: Evidence of controversial Planet 9 uncovered in sky surveys taken 23 years apart
data.author: spchampion2
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了假设中的太阳系行星——第九行星（Planet Nine），该行星最早于2014年被提出，但尚未被正式探测到。天文学家通过一些跨海王星天体（TNOs）的轨道扰动推测其存在。第九行星估计半径是地球的2到4倍，质量约为地球的十倍。2016年，加州理工学院的Michael Brown和Konstantin Batygin提出这一假设，以解释柯伊伯带天体轨道异常聚集的现象。

最近，台湾国立清华大学的天文学家Terry Long Phan团队分析了两次相隔23年的深空红外线观测数据，发现了一个可能的候选对象。该团队使用了1983年IRAS卫星和2006年JAXA的AKARI卫星的数据，通过排除视差效应和快速移动天体，找到了一颗可能的距离太阳约700天文单位的行星。然而，这一发现仍需进一步验证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕假设的第九行星（Planet 9）的各种观点和讨论，包括其距离描述、性质猜测、语法问题以及天文学分类争议。

不同观点：
• 一些评论者关注如何更好地描述假设行星的距离。AIPedant认为用“比冥王星远15倍”比“比地球远700倍”更易于理解，因为这样更能传达出行星距离之远。
• randomtoast提出一个有趣的理论，认为第九行星可能是一个原始黑洞，大小类似于高尔夫球，这可以解释为什么我们只能看到引力效应而无法直接观察到该天体。
• alex_duf对用词提出疑问，认为“farther”应该用于表示实际距离，而“further”则用于比喻意义，反映出对英语用词的困惑。

补充讨论：
• perihelions指出，某些假设和观测结果与Batygin和Brown提出的第九行星假设不符，特别是关于轨道倾角的差异，这引发了对假设天体性质的争议。
• K0balt表达了对原始黑洞理论的偏好，认为这将非常有趣且具有科学价值。
• ashoeafoot将假设行星的轨道比作“巨大的吉他弦”，质疑其受其他天体引力影响的可能性。
• rootsudo对“行星X”变成“行星9”的命名演变感到困惑，这牵涉到冥王星行星地位的变化。
• bikenaga提供了一篇原始论文的链接，试图将讨论引向更科学的依据。
• gitroom调侃了整个讨论的“书呆子”性质，并质疑行星定义的稳定性。
• vpribish对不同天文图像的质量和准确性提出质疑，指出在不同图像中观测结果的不一致。
• _heimdall表达了对冥王星降级的不满，坚持认为冥王星应被视为第九行星。
• anthk和astar1的评论带有幽默和调侃性质，分别提到编程社区和科幻元素（如“质量效应”游戏中的Mass Relay）。
• interludead和tiahura则反思了天文学术语和命名的演变，以及我们对自己太阳系的了解程度。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于假设的第九行星距离和性质的描述，以及天文学命名和分类的一致性问题。

43874641.article_content:
Planet Nine is a hypothesized massive planet, first proposed in 2014, that is speculated to orbit far out in the solar system. It has not been detected formally. Instead, astronomers have inferred its presence from perceived perturbations of the orbits of some Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs). The planet is estimated to be 2 to 4 times the radius, and about ten times the mass of the Earth.
(Image credit: Mark Garlick/Science Photo Library/Getty Images)
The best candidate yet for the elusive Planet Nine has been spotted in two deep infrared surveys taken 23 years apart. If this mystery object really is Planet Nine, it would have a mass greater than Neptune, and currently be about 700 times farther from the sun than Earth is.
The possibility of additional planets in our
solar system
has been proposed many times, going under names such as "Planet X," because experts thought the concept of an extra planet in our vicinity of the cosmos could explain a perceived regularity in mass extinctions on Earth. Perhaps, they said, the periodic influx of
comets
that impact Earth are pushed our way by an unseen planet. However, the supposed periodicity in mass extinctions has not held up to scrutiny, and so the need for that particular Planet X has gone away. This brings us to Planet Nine.
Planet Nine
is unrelated to the Planet X concept, and rather put forward in 2016 by Michael Brown and Konstantin Batygin of the California Institute of Technology to explain an unusual bunching of orbits of some objects in the
Kuiper Belt
, such as Sedna. This proposed Planet Nine would be more massive than
Earth
, and orbit on a highly eccentric path that takes it hundreds of
astronomical units
from the
sun
(one astronomical unit is the distance between Earth and the sun). That far away, it would be extremely difficult to detect.
However, the expectation is that Planet Nine would appear brighter in mid- and far-infrared light than it would in visible light.
You may like
Giant planet or 'failed star?' Newfound mystery world blurs the lines
Scientists discover super-Earth exoplanets are more common in the universe than we thought
Vast swarms of hidden galaxies may be secretly bathing the universe in a soft glow
Now, a team led by astronomer Terry Long Phan of the National Tsing Hua University in Taiwan has delved into the archives of two far-infrared all-sky surveys in search of Planet Nine — and incredibly, they have found something that could possibly be Planet Nine.
The Infrared Astronomy Satellite, IRAS, launched in 1983 and surveyed the
universe
for almost a year before being decommissioned. Then, in 2006, the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched AKARI, another infrared astronomy satellite that was active between 2006 and 2011.
Phan's team were looking for objects that appeared in IRAS's database, then appeared to have moved by the time AKARI took a look. The amount of movement on the sky would be tiny — about three arcminutes per year at a distance of approximately 700 astronomical units (AU). One arcminute is 1/60 of an angular degree.
Get the Space.com Newsletter
Breaking space news, the latest updates on rocket launches, skywatching events and more!
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
But there's an extra motion that Phan's team had to account for. As the Earth orbits the sun, our view of the position of very distant objects changes slightly in an effect called
parallax
. It is the same phenomenon as when you hold your index finger up to your face, close one eye and look at your finger, and then switch eyes — your finger appears to move as a result of you looking at it from a slightly different position.
Planet Nine would appear to move on the sky because of parallax as Earth moves around the sun. On any particular day, it might seem to be in one position, then six months later when Earth is on the other side of the sun, it would shift to another position, perhaps by 10 to 15 arcminutes — then, six months after that, it would seem to shift back to its original position. To remove the effects of parallax, Phan's team searched for Planet Nine on the same date every year in the AKARI data, because on any given date it would appear in the same place, with zero parallax shift, every year.
They then also scrutinized each candidate object that their search threw up on an hourly basis. If a candidate is a fast-moving, nearby object, then its motion would be detectable from hour to hour, and could therefore be ruled out.
This careful search led Phan's team to a single object, a tiny dot in the infrared data.
A comparison of the position of the candidate object in the IRAS data (left) and the AKARI data (right) and the distance in arcminutes between them.
(Image credit: Phan et al (2025))

• ashoeafoot将假设行星的轨道比作“巨大的吉他弦”，质疑其受其他天体引力影响的可能性。
• rootsudo对“行星X”变成“行星9”的命名演变感到困惑，这牵涉到冥王星行星地位的变化。
• bikenaga提供了一篇原始论文的链接，试图将讨论引向更科学的依据。
• gitroom调侃了整个讨论的“书呆子”性质，并质疑行星定义的稳定性。
• vpribish对不同天文图像的质量和准确性提出质疑，指出在不同图像中观测结果的不一致。
• _heimdall表达了对冥王星降级的不满，坚持认为冥王星应被视为第九行星。
• anthk和astar1的评论带有幽默和调侃性质，分别提到编程社区和科幻元素（如“质量效应”游戏中的Mass Relay）。
• interludead和tiahura则反思了天文学术语和命名的演变，以及我们对自己太阳系的了解程度。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于假设的第九行星距离和性质的描述，以及天文学命名和分类的一致性问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MDMA（俗称“摇头丸”或“Ecstasy”）的使用、历史、影响及相关社会问题

不同观点：
• **jimt1234** 分享了20世纪90年代初在加州大学戴维斯分校等地贩卖MDMA的个人经历。他认为当时社会和执法部门对这种药物并不重视，执法宽松，甚至有警察因为私人原因而对其贩卖行为视而不见。他的经历展示了当时MDMA在派对文化中的流行以及执法不严的状况。

• **edweis** 推荐了一本关于LSD制造的 autobiography 《The Rose Of Paracelsus》，将讨论引向对毒品文化的文学探索，特别是对毒品制造历史的深度了解，但没有直接对MDMA的使用发表评价。

• **pas** 引用了关于海洛因成瘾的描述，并暗示长期使用药物可能会损害感受快乐的能力。这一评论带出了对药物长期使用的潜在负面影响的担忧，虽然没有具体针对MDMA，但暗示了药物滥用的普遍问题。

• **ativzzz** 认为MDMA等药物本身可以带来乐趣，但许多人无法以负责任的态度使用药物，导致滥用或过度依赖。他表达了对寻找“负责任的药物使用者”的困惑，并提到成年后如何平衡药物使用与生活的问题。

• **hristov** 提出了MDMA被用作迷奸工具的严重社会问题，并以个人经历讲述了被下药的经历。他警告读者MDMA在某些情况下可能带来的危险，并强调了在使用药物时保持警惕的重要性。他的观点揭示了MDMA在某些场景下的犯罪用途及其潜在的严重后果。

补充讨论：
• MDMA的历史使用背景及其在90年代派对文化中的流行，特别是其与执法系统的互动（jimt1234）。
• 关于药物的文学作品推荐，将讨论拓展至LSD等其他药物（edweis）。
• 对药物滥用的长期生理和心理影响的担忧（pas）。
• 对寻找负责任的药物使用者的讨论，以及成年人如何处理药物与生活的关系（ativzzz）。
• MDMA作为迷奸工具的严重社会问题及其潜在的法律与个人安全影响（hristov）。

争议焦点：
• MDMA是否能够负责任地使用。ativzzz认为存在负责任的使用方式，但现实中许多人滥用；hristov则通过个人经历表明MDMA在某些场景下被滥用作犯罪工具，强调其危险性。
• 执法部门对MDMA的态度。jimt1234提到90年代执法不严，而hristov则指出当代MDMA相关的犯罪问题。

data.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕2018年上传到GitHub的 bootloader 源代码及其历史、技术细节和实用性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [1vuio0pswjnm7] 认为Hacker News (HN) 标题中添加的"(2018)"不准确，因为该 bootloader 的源代码早在2012年就上传到了Google，2018年的版本只是增加了注释。他还提供了相关的历史存档链接和额外技术文档以支持他的观点。

• [D4ckard] 对MBR（主引导记录）的 hack 表示兴趣，并通过引用 Sector Lisp 和 OSle 项目来展示他对类似技术的好奇和支持。

• [gitroom] 认为旧的 bootloader 技术仍然有效令人印象深刻，并表示这种持久性让研究它变得值得，隐含了对技术稳定性的欣赏。

• [6SixTy] 认为该 bootloader 仅支持 BIOS/MBR 限制了其吸引力，暗示现代系统可能需要更先进的解决方案。

• [micw] 关注其实用性，提出每次在新内核上使用时是否需要重新编译和安装的问题，显示出对维护成本的关心。

• [M95D] 质疑该 bootloader 相对于 Lilo（另一种引导程序）的优势，表明他可能更偏好使用其他更成熟或更高效的工具。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到对技术历史的澄清，特别是源代码上传时间和版本差异。
• 对 bootloader 技术的怀旧和技术兴趣，通过具体项目（如 Sector Lisp 和 OSle）的引用展示出来。
• 对 bootloader 在现代系统中的适用性和实用性存在一定争议，部分用户对其局限性表示失望。
• 关注技术实现中的具体问题，如内核更新时的重新编译需求，反映了实际使用中的挑战。

争议焦点：该 bootloader 相对于其他工具（如 Lilo）的优势以及其在现代计算环境中的适用性。

data.title: The Speed of VITs and CNNs
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了视觉Transformer（ViT）和卷积神经网络（CNN）在计算机视觉任务中的速度和扩展性。作者通过实验证明，ViT在分辨率高达1024x1024px²时表现良好，并且在许多现代GPU上速度优于CNN。实验包括在不同设备和批量大小上进行基准测试，结果显示ViT在推理速度、FLOPs和内存使用方面具有优势。作者还指出，高分辨率对于大多数图像处理任务并不必要，常见场景如自然图像和文本图像在较低分辨率下即可满足需求。ViT和CNN的性能差异不仅仅体现在FLOPs上，还涉及实际运行速度和内存效率。总体而言，ViT在扩展性和实用性方面表现优异，适用于大多数计算机视觉任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LeCun关于高分辨率图像和VITs（Vision Transformers）适用性的评论引发的讨论

不同观点：
• John7878781：认为LeCun的评论并非如文章所说的"轻率反应"。他指出1024x1024不应被视为高分辨率，尤其是在处理需要极高细节的图像（如4096x2048）时，CNN（如convnext）比VITs更为实用。
• jacobgorm：强调CNNs在推理时可以改变分辨率而不需要重新训练，比如适应不同摄像头或手机方向。质疑VITs是否能在不重新训练的情况下支持分辨率或纵横比的变化。
• kookamamie：同意1024x1024不属于高分辨率，并举例1920x1080（FHD）视频的分割任务，强调高分辨率的必要性。
• ninamoss：支持VITs的使用，表示通过模型编译和超参数调整，VITs能够在普通硬件上实现高精度和快速评估。
• GaggiX：质疑文章中关于448px²足够处理文本和图表的论断，指出提供的图表例子中448px²并不足够。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于什么是“高分辨率”以及在不同应用场景下CNNs和VITs的适用性。John7878781和kookamamie都认为1024x1024不算高分辨率，而ninamoss则分享了VITs在一些应用中的成功经验。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是CNNs在处理不同分辨率和纵横比时的灵活性，jacobgorm对此提出疑问，而VITs在这方面的表现尚不明确。
• 具体应用场景（如文本、图表处理）中分辨率需求的不同也引发了对CNNs和VITs优劣的进一步讨论。

43866329.article_content:
On the speed of ViTs and CNNs
You disabled JavaScript.
Please enable it for syntax-highlighting, or don't complain about unlegible code snippets =)
This page doesn't contain any tracking/analytics/ad code.
Context
Computer vision is now powered by two workhorse architectures:
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Vision Transformers (ViT).
CNNs slide a feature extractor (stack of convolutions) over the image
to get the final, usually lower-resolution, feature map on which the task is performed.
ViTs on the other hand cut the image into patches from the start and perform stacks
of self-attention on all the patches, leading to the final feature map, also of lower resolution.
It is often stated that because of the quadratic self-attention,
ViTs aren't practical at higher resolution.
As the most prominent example, here is Yann LeCun, Godfather of CNNs, stating the following:
However, I believe this criticism is a misguided knee-jerk reaction and, in practice,
ViTs scale perfectly fine up to at least 1024x1024px², which is enough for the vast
majority of usage scenarios for image encoders.
In this article, I make two points:
ViTs scale just fine up to at least 1024x1024px²
For the vast majority of uses, that resolution is more than enough.
ViTs scale just fine with resolution
First, I set out to quantify the inference speed of plain ViTs and CNNs on a range of current GPUs.
To give this benchmark as wide an appeal as possible, I stray away from my usual JAX+TPU toolbox
and perform benchmarking using PyTorch on a few common GPUs.
I use models from the de-facto standard vision model repository
timm
,
and
follow PyTorch best practices in terms of benchmarking and performance
by using
torch.compile
.
I further sweep over dtype (
float32
,
float16
,
bfloat16
),
attention implementation (
sdpa_kernel
),
and matmul precision (
set_float32_matmul_precision
)
and take the best setting among all these for each measurement.
Since I am quite rusty in PyTorch, here is my
full benchmarking code
,
and I'll be glad to take feedback from experts.
Besides just speed, I also compute
FLOPs
and measure peak memory usage.
Thanks to
RunPod
for providing the compute and making the benchmarking easy.
I benchmarked various devices:
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
and batch-sizes:
1
|
8
|
32
, so take your pick.
(
ViTDet
, for later
)
Now that you've browsed these measurements a bit, I hope we get to the same conclusions:
ViT's scale just fine with resolution, at least up to 1024px².
Often times ViT is faster than an equivalent CNN, especially on more modern GPUs.
FLOPs
!= speed, see also my
Efficiency Misnomer
paper with Mostafa, Yi, Anurag, and Ashish on the topic.
Out of the box
1
, ViT is more memory-efficient. On the GTX3070, it is
the only
model that can go beyond 512px².
But wait, it gets better! We already had all of this in the original ViT paper.
We've successfully
scaled ResNets before anyone else
,
and were most annoyed by memory. So we (me, specifically) included this figure in the appendix:
This figure was on TPUv3, i.e. a few generations ago. This blogpost is on various current GPUs.
I think it is safe to say that these are universal take-aways between ViTs and CNNs by now;
they have stood the test of time.
You don't need very high resolution
My second argument is that people waste too much of their time focussing on resolution,
aspect ratio, and related things.
My
conservative
claim is that you can always stretch to a square, and for:
natural images, meaning most photos, 224px² is enough;
text in photos, phone screens, diagrams and charts, 448px² is enough;
desktop screens and single-page documents, 896px² is enough.
(Yes, you recoginized correctly, these are the
PaliGemma
numbers.
That's no coincidence.)
Higher resolutions exist purely for human consumption: for the aesthetic beauty of very crisp lines, and to avoid eye strain.
However, computer vision models do not suffer from eye strain, and do not care about aesthetic beauty.
At least for now, while AI is not yet sentient.
There are a few very special exceptions, including medical and satellite images or multi-page documents.
I believe these can be split into pieces of any of the above sizes, with
maybe
a light global feature.
But I am no expert in those.
The most important thing is to always look at your data, the same way your model will see it.
If you can solve your task looking at it, even with effort, then so can your model.
Let's do this for a few representative images:

data.title: Nevermind, an album on major chords
data.author: lozzo
data.article_summary: 《Nevermind》专辑在1991年意外成为音乐界的轰动之作，其粗犷的吉他、独特的喊叫式演唱和原始的音色吸引了大量听众。尽管大多数人只是享受音乐，并未深入分析其艺术性。如今，30多年过去，文章揭示了该专辑令人难忘的几个特殊元素。专辑大量使用强力和弦，主要为大调和弦，且和声进程不拘于传统音阶，几乎没有小调和复杂和弦。这种简约而创新的手法在每首歌中都得以体现，尽管科特·科本自称不懂乐理，仅凭音乐直觉创作，但正是这种独特的方式造就了《Nevermind》的非凡影响力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kurt Cobain及Nirvana音乐中的和弦使用与音乐理论分析

不同观点：
• mingus88认为Kurt Cobain主要使用强力和弦（power chords），这些和弦既不是大调也不是小调，因为缺乏三音。这种和弦使用在朋克和金属中很常见，且朋克音乐本质上是DIY（自己动手）的，没有固定的规则。将Cobain捧为音乐天才是不合适的，因为分析朋克音乐时使用古典西方调性是荒谬且做作的。
• florilegiumson指出在分析Nirvana的音乐时，和弦进程可能存在错误。虽然乐队主要使用强力和弦，但Cobain的演唱中包含的三音会影响和弦的听感，例如《Smells Like Teen Spirit》实际听起来像F小调。确定流行音乐的调性是困难的，因为和弦进程通常很简单，且缺乏古典音乐中的目的性。
• crucialfelix认为Cobain和其他朋克音乐人一样，实际上是懂和弦的，但他追求一种天真、原始的声音。Cobain自称不懂音乐理论是为了符合朋克文化的反叛形象。这种文化在70年代的Discharge、Wire、Fugazi等乐队中已经存在。
• SwellJoe强烈反对将Cobain捧为音乐天才，指出强力和弦没有大调或小调的特性，它们在朋克和摇滚乐中早已存在。Cobain是一个优秀的摇滚歌曲作者，但并不是特别创新或技术上独一无二的。

补充讨论：
• marko-djuric和eimrine对讨论的主题感到困惑，不确定讨论的是GitHub页面HTML还是音乐理论。
• tim333指出在《Smells Like Teen Spirit》这首歌中，每隔几秒就有一个听起来不太符合小调的次要和弦。
• cue_the_strings提到Nirvana的歌曲中，Cobain经常通过演唱旋律来加入三音，且当时的文化倾向于假装缺乏音乐理论知识，这种做法在当时具有一定的破坏性。
• codazoda推荐了Dave Grohl的《The Storyteller》一书，认为这本书对Nirvana及其音乐影响有很好的描述。
• jsphweid详细分析了Cobain的吉他演奏方式，指出他使用食指和无名指的特殊和弦按法，这种按法会导致和弦在大调与非大调之间产生模糊的音感，并指出了某些和弦分析中的错误。
• fuhsnn提到自60年代迷幻摇滚以来，全三和弦的半音大调和弦已经存在，因此不需要用强力和弦来解释大调和弦的存在，如The Rolling Stones的音乐。

争议焦点：
• Kurt Cobain是否在和弦使用上具有创新性，以及是否应该用古典音乐理论分析朋克和摇滚音乐。
• 《Smells Like Teen Spirit》等Nirvana歌曲的具体调性分析，尤其是强力和弦与演唱旋律之间的关系。

May, 2025
Nevermind, an album on major chords
🎵 Back in 1991, Nevermind become an unexpected critical and commercial sensation.
Its raw guitars and rough, unapologetic sound captivated listeners,
though most of us simply enjoyed it without appreciating its artistry.
Scream like singing

Careful music analysis was left for other bands.
Now, more than 30 years later, I want to uncover a few special ingredients that made it truly unforgettable.
Please take a few minutes to listen to each excerpt below
Buried under distorted overdriven guitars,
one song at the time,
a music made of new innovative harmonic idioms emerges.
Power chords - mostly sounding as Major chords - in harmonic progressions outside any scale.
Hardly any minor chord and no fancy chords (7th, 2nd, 4th, 6th, 9th, dim, aug).
And it was like this for every song in Nevermind. Surely, other singers and bands, way before nirvana, had written songs using similar techniques,
but those would have been a few tracks in otherwise standard rock albums.
In 1991, Kurt Cobain wrote an album with just major chords
And it's fascinating to think that Kurt Cobain was unaware of any musical composition's rule he was following, but just trusting his musical instict.
I have no
concept of knowing how to be a musician at all, whatsoever,
(I mean) I don't know the names of the chords to play
I don't know how to do major and minor chords on a guitar at all...

data.title: The complicated business of electing a Doge
data.author: dr_dshiv
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了威尼斯总督选举的复杂流程，该流程在1268年至威尼斯共和国结束的约五百年间基本未变。首先，从威尼斯大议会中抽签选出三十名成员，再从中抽签选出九人，这九人提名四十名候选人。之后经过多轮抽签和筛选，候选人数逐步减少并重新提名，最终由四十一人的选举团选出总督。选举需获得至少二十五个赞成票才能获胜。整个过程涉及多次抽签和复杂的提名程序，被形容为繁琐、荒诞而又深奥。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：威尼斯选举制度及其历史背景和现代反思

不同观点：
• [历史视角] simonebrunozzi指出威尼斯共和国的持续时间长达1100年，比历史上任何其他共和国都长。他认为选举制度是其长久存在的原因之一，并提到如果不是拿破仑，威尼斯共和国可能仍然存在。

• [术语解释] Nezteb通过链接解释了“Doge”这一称号的含义，提供了基本背景信息。

• [学术分析] PhilipRoman分享了一个关于13世纪威尼斯选举制度的严谨分析，提供了深入研究该主题的学术资源。

• [抽签治理] dr_dshiv介绍了“抽签”（Sortition）的概念，指出其在古雅典的根源，并将这一概念与威尼斯的选举制度联系起来。

• [制度细节疑问] thinkingemote对选举过程中的具体操作提出疑问，例如选举池是否变化，是否有人可以多次被选中等，寻求更详细的解释或示例。

• [选举的消极面] AdamN提到两个有趣的元观点：候选人未必想成为Doge，因为这对他们的独立性和财富可能有负面影响；另外，一位试图成为国王的Doge被永远记住，这显示了威尼斯对权力集中的警惕。

• [历史背景与神意] Telemakhos补充了选举制度发展的历史背景，指出1268年制度的建立是为了解决派系斗争问题。他还提到神意在选举中的潜在影响，认为随机选择与神意结合可能被认为能带来最佳结果。

• [系统漏洞] NemoNobody认为威尼斯的选举过程非常复杂且怪异，虽然可能存在漏洞，但从外部难以察觉。

• [历史趣闻] crop_rotation分享了一个与威尼斯Doge相关的历史趣闻，提到第一个被葬在伊斯坦布尔圣索菲亚大教堂的人是威尼斯的Doge。

• [重复选举问题] meew0对选举中是否允许重复选择之前被选中的人提出疑问，认为这可能导致寡头政治。

• [现代反思] dostick反思现代选举制度的不足，提出在计算机时代，直接为议题和原因投票而非通过中间代表的想法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于威尼斯选举制度的复杂性和潜在的操作性问题，特别是随机选择和重复选举的可能性对制度公正性的影响。
• 讨论还涉及威尼斯选举制度的历史发展和其在现代背景下的反思与改进可能。

通过这些观点，我们可以看到对威尼斯选举制度的多元理解，包括其历史意义、具体操作细节、潜在问题及现代反思。

43888777.article_content:
The Complicated Business of Electing a Doge
“
Whenever the time came to elect a new doge of Venice, an official went to pray in St. Mark’s Basilica, grabbed the first boy he could find in the piazza, and took him back to the ducal palace. The boy’s job was to draw lots to choose an electoral college from the members of Venice’s grand families, which was the first step in a performance that has been called tortuous, ridiculous, and profound. Here is how it went, more or less unchanged, for five hundred years, from 1268 until the end of the Venetian Republic.
Thirty electors were chosen by lot, and then a second lottery reduced them to nine, who nominated forty candidates in all, each of whom had to be approved by at least seven electors in order to pass to the next stage. The forty were pruned by lot to twelve, who nominated a total of twenty-five, who needed at least nine nominations each. The twenty-five were culled to nine, who picked an electoral college of forty-five, each with at least seven nominations. The forty-five became eleven, who chose a final college of forty-one. Each member proposed one candidate, all of whom were discussed and, if necessary, examined in person, whereupon each elector cast a vote for every candidate of whom he approved. The candidate with the most approvals was the winner, provided he had been endorsed by at least twenty-five of the forty-one.
”
— Anthony Gottlieb, "Win or Lose," The New Yorker.
Thirty members of the Great Council, chosen by lot, were reduced by lot to nine; the nine chose forty and the forty were reduced by lot to twelve, who chose twenty-five. The twenty-five were reduced by lot to nine, and the nine elected forty-five. The forty-five were reduced by lot to eleven, and the eleven chose the forty-one who elected the doge. Election required at least twenty-five votes out of forty-one.

data.title: Typed Lisp, a Primer
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了Lisp的类型系统，特别是与Haskell的对比，并通过具体例子展示了Lisp中代数多态类型（如Pair和Maybe）的定义和异构类型列表的处理。文章首先简要对比了Haskell和Lisp的类型系统，接着介绍了Lisp的类型理论及一些技术细节，如类型层次结构和类型声明。Lisp的类型系统允许类型重叠，其基本类型包括整数、字符串、列表、向量等。文章还讨论了类型的逻辑操作（如联合、交集、补集等），并通过代码示例展示了这些类型的使用。最终，文章展示了通过宏实现类似Haskell的类型声明，并表达了对Lisp优雅特性的赞赏，旨在吸引熟悉Haskell的程序员尝试Lisp。

• breadchris也欣赏Lisp，尤其是Clojure，但强调了强类型系统的重要性，认为这能增强开发的信心。

Typed Lisp, A Primer
21 Aug 2019
Abstract
Let's explore Lisp's fine-grained type hierarchy!
We begin with a shallow comparison to Haskell, a rapid tour of type theory,
try in vain to defend dynamic approaches, give a somewhat humorous account of history,
note that you've been bamboozled —type's have always been there—,
then go into technical details of some Lisp types, and finally conclude by showing
how
macros permit typing
.
Goals for this article:
Multiple examples of type constructions in Lisp.
Comparing Lisp type systems with modern languages, such as Haskell.
Show how algebraic
polymorphic
types like
Pair
and
Maybe
can be defined in Lisp.
Including heterogeneously typed lists!
Convey a passion for an elegant language.
Augment Lisp with functional Haskell-like type declarations ;-)
Unless suggested otherwise, the phrase “Lisp” refers to
Common Lisp as supported by Emacs Lisp
. As such, the resulting discussion
is applicable to a number of Lisp dialects
—I'm ignoring editing types such as buffers and keymaps, for now.
( Original print by Baneen Al-hassy as a birthday present to me. )
1
“Loving Haskell & Lisp is Inconsistent”
I have convinced a number of my peers to use Emacs/Spacemacs/Doom-emacs,
but my efforts to get them to even consider trying Lisp have been met with
staunch rejection. These peers are familiar with Haskell, and almost all know Agda,
so you'd think they'd be willing to try Lisp —it's there, part of their editor—
but the superficial chasm in terms of syntax and types is more than enough apparently.
In this article, I aim to explore the type system of (Emacs) Lisp and occasionally
make comparisons to Haskell. Perhaps in the end some of my Haskell peers would be
willing to try it out.
Figure 1:
xkcd - Lisp is a language of timeless elegance
↯ I almost never use Haskell for any day-to-day dealings.
✓ The ideas expressed by its community are why I try
to keep updated on the language.
↯ No one around me knows anything about Lisp,
but they dislike it due to the parens.
✓ I love it and use it for Emacs configuration and recently
to prototype my PhD research.
⇅ I love that I can express a complicated procedure compactly in both
by using zips, unzips, filters, and maps
(งಠ_ಠ)ง
Lately, in Lisp, I'll write a nested loop (gasp!)
then, for fun, try to make it a one-liner!
Sometimes, I actually think the loop formulation is clearer
and I leave it as a loop —Breaking news: Two Haskell readers just died.
Figure 2:
From the awesome “Land of Lisp” book
What I like and why:
Haskell
⇒
Executable category theory; compact & eloquent
Lisp
⇒
Extensible language; malleable, uniform, beautiful
Documentation?
Haskell
⇒
Hoogle; can search by type alone!
Emacs Lisp
⇒
Self-documenting;
M-x apropos
How has using the language affected me?
Haskell
I almost always think in-terms compoistionality, functors, & currying
Lisp
Documentation strings, units tests, and metaprogramming are second nature
It may not be entirely accurate to say that
Lisp's type system is more expressive than Haskell's
as it's orthogonal in many respects; although it is closer to that of
Liquid Haskell
.
2
Why Bother with Types? A Terse Tutorial on Type Systems
Types allow us to treat objects according a similar structure
or interface.
Unlike Haskell and other statically typed systems, in Lisp we have
that types can overlap.
As such, here's our working definition.
A
type
is a collection of possible objects.
To say “\(e\) has type \(τ\)” one writes \(e : τ\), or in Lisp:
(typep e 'τ)
.
Haskellers and others may append to this definition the following,
which we will not bother with:
Type membership is determined by inspecting
syntactic structure and so is decidable.
✓ Typing is one of the simplest forms of “assertion-comments”:
Documenting a property of your code in a way that the machine can verify.
If you're gonna comment on what kind of thing you're working with, why not have the
comment checked by the machine.
Table 1:
Lisp's type hierarchy is a “complemented lattice” ♥‿♥

integer, number, string, keyword, array, cons, list, vector, macro, function, atom

not
of type
τ

is the type consisting of only the elements
xᵢ
Singleton
(eql x)
is the type with only the element
x
Comprehension
(satisfies p)
is the type of values that satisfy predicate
p

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程中的代码美学、可读性以及编程中不变的问题

不同观点：
• [blendo] 认为更具“美感”的代码通常更具可读性。他基于自己自1980年以来的编程经验，提出这一观点，暗示代码的视觉美感与其实用性（可读性）之间存在关联。

• [Jtsummers] 引用了Gerald Weinberg的著作《The Psychology of Computer Programming》，指出Weinberg在团队编程和相关主题上的研究，特别是如何评估编程实践和团队合作中的有效性，这与视频中的内容相关。

• [gitroom] 支持Weinberg的观点，尤其对团队动力学有共鸣，并提出一个开放性问题：无论技术如何变化，传统编程中的问题是否永远存在。这暗示了编程中的一些挑战可能是普遍且持久的。

• [Topgamer7] 用幽默的方式指出，代码或文档难以理解的问题可能自古就有，甚至可以追溯到庞贝古城的时代。这暗示了沟通不清或复杂性问题可能在各种时代和背景下都会出现。

• [reader9274] 以幽默回应Python语言的能力，指出虽然程序员无法让计算机理解代码的缩进格式，但Python语言本身却能处理这一问题。这暗示了某些现代编程语言在设计上已经考虑到了代码美学和可读性的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了Gerald Weinberg的著作及其在编程心理学和团队合作方面的见解，强调了编程中的社会和心理因素。
• 另一个重要的讨论点是关于编程中长期存在的问题，即无论技术如何进步，某些问题似乎仍然存在，这引发对编程本质问题的思考。
• 最后，通过幽默的方式提出了编程语言（如Python）在代码可读性和格式处理上的进步，表明技术在一定程度上已经回应了这些美学和可读性的需求。

data.title: Technical analysis of the Signal clone used by Trump officials
data.author: micahflee
data.article_summary: 本文披露了特朗普政府官员使用的一款非官方Signal应用程序（TM SGNL），该程序由TeleMessage公司开发，能够自动存档明文聊天记录。尽管使用Signal的服务器进行端到端加密通讯，TM SGNL会在发送和接收消息时将明文副本存档，可能违反Signal的开放源代码许可协议。TeleMessage的高管多有以色列国防军情报部门背景，其应用程序未公开下载，仅通过企业设备管理服务提供。文章还提到，TM SGNL可能违反GNU Affero通用公共许可证，因其未公开修改后的源代码。TeleMessage还开发了类似存档功能的WhatsApp、Telegram和WeChat应用程序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal加密通信系统的安全性及其在政府机构中的使用，特别是关于Telemark的TM SGNL应用的争议。

不同观点：
• **对使用TM SGNL的质疑**：
  - **abhisek**：对将E2E加密通信存档到破坏安全模型的存储中表示不解，认为这违背了使用Signal的初衷，使得他人能够搜索所有信息。
  - **throw7**：质疑Signal是否正式允许另一个构建（TM SGNL）访问Signal网络。
  - **ComputerGuru**：提到Signal是政府官员被批准使用的应用，但未听说TeleMessage被批准，并对外国情报因素表示关注。

• **对数据控制和存档的需求**：
  - **jFriedensreich**：认为E2E加密通讯限制了用户对数据的控制，违反了数据可移植性权利，建议强制通讯应用提供API访问并显示警告。

• **对TeleMessage公司背景的关注**：
  - **mdhb**：强调TeleMessage由前以色列情报官员控制，认为这可能带来安全风险。

• **对政府使用Signal及第三方应用的态度**：
  - **jimmydoe**：认为特朗普政府遵守法律进行聊天存档是令人放心的，但对以色列公司的不专业表示不满。
  - **be_erik**：认为公共官员不应使用Signal，但Signal技术本身是优秀的，问题在于使用方式和管理。

• **对Signal功能改进的建议**：
  - **macrolime**：指出TM SGNL存在是因为Signal没有在iPhone上存档消息的功能，建议Signal考虑添加此功能。

• **对TM SGNL应用外观的讨论**：
  - **jcgl**：询问TM SGNL与官方Signal应用在视觉上的区别。

• **对决策责任的质疑**：
  - **LordShredda**：认为使用Signal替代品是经过计划和管理的决定，质疑谁负责管理这些手机。

• **对美国政府IT决策的批评**：
  - **senectus1**：批评美国政府使用修改过的Signal版本，认为这破坏了Signal的加密优势，是极其不明智的做法。

• **新发展的报道**：
  - **spenvo**：提到有报道称TeleMessage公司被黑客入侵，认为这是重要的新动态，应重新考虑之前的讨论决定。

补充讨论：
- 评论中对Telemark的TM SGNL应用的安全性、合法性及外国背景提出了广泛质疑和关注。
- 对Signal本身的技术优势和其在政府使用中的实际风险有不同看法，部分人认为问题不在于Signal技术，而在于第三方应用和管理决策。
- 出现了对数据存档需求与加密安全之间矛盾的讨论，以及对政府IT决策透明度和安全性的担忧。

💡
Update May 3, 2025:
I have posted a follow-up,
Here's the source code for the unofficial Signal app used by Trump officials
.
Yesterday, a Reuters photographer captured a
photo
of the freshly-ousted former National Security Advisor Mike Waltz checking his Signal messages during a Trump cabinet meeting. If you're not familiar with Waltz, he's most well known for inviting The Atlantic's editor-in-chief to secret Trump administration
war crimes Signal group
. They discussed, and executed, bombing an urban apartment building full of civilians to kill a single man.
404 Media journalist Joseph Cox
published a story
pointing out that Waltz was not using the official Signal app, but rather "an obscure and unofficial version of Signal that is designed to archive messages" called TM SGNL.
Zoomed-in crop of the Reuters photo showing Mike Waltz using the TM SGNL app. Images credit: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein
This app uses Signal's servers, making it possible for Waltz to send end-to-end encrypted messages to normal Signal users, like Jeffrey Goldberg from The Atlantic, for example. However unlike the Signal end of the encrypted conversation, the TM SGNL end automatically archives a copy of the plaintext messages (even ones with disappearing messages) somewhere else that may or may not be secure.
In a
video
the company published, they show Signal messages getting archived into a Gmail account.
I decided to look into this app. I discovered:
The senior executives of the company behind TM SGNL appear to be Israeli, and the CEO's bio mentions his work with Israel Defense Forces' Intelligence unit.
TM SGNL is most likely violating Signal's open source license, and the company's other apps are probably violating the proprietary licenses of other software like WhatsApp and WeChat.
The Android and iOS versions of the app are not available for the public to download, and in fact practically the only way to get the app is if you're using a device enrolled in an MDM service that's tied to an Apple Business Manager or Google Enterprise account.
I speculate about exactly how I think the Trump administration is using this (unapproved for classified info) app to discuss classified info, and how they are likely managing their fleet of iPhones.
Finally, I share a PDF and a video I discovered that go into detail about, among other things, where the chat logs may be stored.
Before I get started, consider
subscribing
to get these posts emailed directly to your inbox. If you want to support my work, considering becoming a paid supporter.
The company behind TM SGNL
The TM SGNL app is part of a suite of apps by a company called
TeleMessage
, which is owned by
Smarsh
, a company that makes e-discovery software, which is basically software designed for police and lawyers and whatnot to search archives of data.
I haven't spent a lot of time looking into TeleMessage, but what I did find at a quick glance is that several of the executives on the
teams page
list Israeli universities in their bios, and the CEO, Guy Levit, says that, "From 1996 until 1999, Guy served as the head of the planning and development of one of the IDF’s Intelligence elite technical units."
How the app probably works
Based on the photo of Waltz's screen, TM SGNL is most likely a version of Signal that is slightly modified. The app name is changed from "Signal" to "TM SGNL" (which is why Walt'z screen says, "Verify your TM SGNL PIN" instead of "Verify your Signal PIN").
And there is most likely an additional piece of code that gets executed whenever a message is sent or received which forwards the plaintext version of that message to the "corporate archive," as the company calls it.
TM SGNL might be violating Signal's open source licenses
Signal is open source. Here's the
Signal-iOS
code and here's the
Signal-Android
code. Because the code is available, creating an app like TM SGNL would actually be pretty easy to do.
Signal has done all of the hard work in making an end-to-end encryption messaging app. Signal also runs the server infrastructure. The TeleMessage devs simply have to clone the git repos of the client apps, figure out where to insert the archiving code, and make their own separate releases.
The Signal apps are licensed under the
GNU Affero General Public License
, a copyleft license that allows anyone to make modified versions (like TM SGNL) provided that they also use the same open source license. The license text says that when making modifications to the source code:
You must license the entire work, as a whole, under this License to anyone who comes into possession of a copy.
So, if someone has a copy of TM SGNL, they should be able to request that TeleMessage provide a copy of the source code, which should also be open source, and if TeleMessage does not comply they will be violating Signal's license – essentially, selling pirated software.
TeleMessage also publishes similar apps for WhatsApp, Telegram, and even WeChat, that probably work in similar ways. B

  - **jFriedensreich**：认为E2E加密通讯限制了用户对数据的控制，违反了数据可移植性权利，建议强制通讯应用提供API访问并显示警告。

• **对TeleMessage公司背景的关注**：
  - **mdhb**：强调TeleMessage由前以色列情报官员控制，认为这可能带来安全风险。

• **对政府使用Signal及第三方应用的态度**：
  - **jimmydoe**：认为特朗普政府遵守法律进行聊天存档是令人放心的，但对以色列公司的不专业表示不满。
  - **be_erik**：认为公共官员不应使用Signal，但Signal技术本身是优秀的，问题在于使用方式和管理。

• **对Signal功能改进的建议**：
  - **macrolime**：指出TM SGNL存在是因为Signal没有在iPhone上存档消息的功能，建议Signal考虑添加此功能。

• **对TM SGNL应用外观的讨论**：
  - **jcgl**：询问TM SGNL与官方Signal应用在视觉上的区别。

• **对决策责任的质疑**：
  - **LordShredda**：认为使用Signal替代品是经过计划和管理的决定，质疑谁负责管理这些手机。

• **对美国政府IT决策的批评**：
  - **senectus1**：批评美国政府使用修改过的Signal版本，认为这破坏了Signal的加密优势，是极其不明智的做法。

• **新发展的报道**：
  - **spenvo**：提到有报道称TeleMessage公司被黑客入侵，认为这是重要的新动态，应重新考虑之前的讨论决定。

补充讨论：
- 评论中对Telemark的TM SGNL应用的安全性、合法性及外国背景提出了广泛质疑和关注。
- 对Signal本身的技术优势和其在政府使用中的实际风险有不同看法，部分人认为问题不在于Signal技术，而在于第三方应用和管理决策。
- 出现了对数据存档需求与加密安全之间矛盾的讨论，以及对政府IT决策透明度和安全性的担忧。

data.title: Why Archers Didn't Volley Fire
data.author: StefanBatory
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了影视作品中常见的视觉元素——齐射箭阵，并指出其多处错误。首先，命令弓箭手“开火”是不准确的，因为弓箭不涉及火焰。其次，历史上弓箭手并不进行齐射，他们根据自己的最佳时机射击，形成“箭雨”或“箭雹”。这种齐射在实际战斗中既无必要也无法实现，因为弓箭的重新装填时间不如火枪那样需要通过齐射来弥补。此外，即使齐射，其效果也不会像影视中展现的那样具有毁灭性。文章还提到，齐射战术主要用于解决火枪等武器装填慢的问题，通过轮流射击保持火力连续性。最后，作者邀请读者通过Patreon支持其项目，并提供社交媒体更新。

43877644.article_content:
Bret Devereaux
Collections
May 2, 2025
May 2, 2025
30 Minutes
This week we’re looking at a specific visual motif common in TV and film: the arrow volley.  You know the scene: the general readies his archers, he orders them to ‘draw!’ and then holds up his hand with that ‘wait for it’ gesture and then shouts ‘loose!’ (or worse yet, ‘fire!’) and all of the archers release at once, producing a giant cloud of arrows.  And then those arrows hit the enemy, with whole ranks collapsing and wounded soldiers falling over everywhere.
From Alexander (2004) showing the Battle of Gaugamela.  This bit is amazing because Darius III
silently gestures
and all of his archers draw their bows (also why are they kneeling? They’re shooting at a high angle! There’s no need to kneel!) and then at another
silent gesture
which they
cannot see
because Darius III is
behind them
, they all release at once.
And every part of that scene is wrong
.
Now the thing that, in the last couple of decades,
everyone
has realized is wrong (I suspect some early Lindybeige videos had something to do with how widespread this notion is), is that you don’t tell archers to ‘fire’ because their weapons
don’t involve any fire
.  But the solution in film has been to keep the arrow
volleys
– that is, the coordinated all-at-once shooting – and simply change the order to ‘release’ or ‘loose.’  Which isn’t actually any better!
Archers didn’t engage in coordinated all-at-once shooting (called ‘volley fire’), they did not shoot in volleys because there wouldn’t be any point to do so.  Indeed, part of the reason there was such confusion over what a general is supposed to shout instead of ‘fire!’ is that historical tactical manuals don’t generally have commands for coordinated bow shooting
because armies didn’t do coordinated bow shooting
.
Instead, archers generated a ‘hail’ or ‘rain’ (those are the typical metaphors) of arrows as each archer shot in their own best time
.
More to the point, they
could not
shoot in volleys. And even if they
had
shot in volleys, those volleys wouldn’t produce
anything
like the impact we regularly see in film or TV.
So this week, we’re going to walk through those considerations
: briefly looking at what volley fire is for and why archers both wouldn’t and couldn’t do it, before taking a longer look at the problem of
lethality
in massed arrow fire.
But first, if you want to help support this project you can do so on
Patreon
!  I don’t promise to use your money to buy myself more arms and armor, but I also don’t promise
not
to do that.  And if you want updates whenever a new post appears, you can click below for email updates or follow me on Twitter (@BretDevereaux) and Bluesky (@bretdevereaux.bsky.social) and (less frequently) Mastodon (@bretdevereaux@historians.social) for updates when posts go live and my general musings; I have largely shifted over to Bluesky (I maintain some
de minimis
presence on Twitter), given that it has become a much better place for historical discussion than Twitter.
Email Address
Subscribe!
What Is Volley Fire For?
We want to start by understanding what volley fire
is
and what it is
for
. Put simply, ‘volley fire’ is the tactic of having a whole bunch of soldiers with ranged weapons (typically guns) fire in coordinated groups: sometimes with the entire unit all firing at once or with specific sub-components of the unit firing in coordinated fashion, as with the ‘counter-march.’ In both cases, the problem that volley fire is trying to overcome is
slow weapon reload times
: this is a solution for
slow-firing
but
powerful
ranged weapons. That has generally meant firearms, historically, but we do actually see volley fire drill with crossbows in China from a very early period as well (but, interestingly, there’s no evidence I am aware of that volley fire was ever done with crossbows in Europe – when Europeans decide to do volley fire with firearms, it seems to have been an entirely new idea).
1
From The Two Towers (2002).  Théoden here has been having his archers
hold their shots
for going on a couple of minutes at this point, so while volley fire with arrows is stupid, he’s probably right that he’s only going to give the enemy one volley before his archers collapse from exhaustion.
Volley fire can cover for the slow reload rate of guns or crossbows in two ways. The first are volley fire drills designed to ensure a continuous curtain of fire; the most famous of these is the ‘counter-march,’ a drill where arquebuses or muskets are deployed several ranks deep (as many as six). The front rank fires a volley (that is, they all fire together) and then rush to the back of their file to begin reloading, allowing the next rank to fire, and so on. By the time the last rank has fired, the whole formation has moved backwards slightly (thus ‘counter’ march) and the first rank has finished reloading and is ready to fire. data.title: How Riot Games is fighting the war against video game hackers
data.author: badmonster
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了视频游戏中的作弊问题以及游戏公司如何打击作弊行为。随着网络竞技的发展，作弊已成为一个利润丰厚的产业，作弊者通过销售不公平的优势获利。为了应对这一问题，游戏开发商加强了反作弊团队，其中Riot Games开发的Vanguard反作弊系统尤为突出。Vanguard在操作系统内核层面运行，能够深入监控玩家的电脑，每天禁言大量作弊者。Riot利用Windows的安全功能，检查硬件驱动程序更新，防止作弊软件加载和执行代码。此外，Riot还通过渗透作弊社区、使用虚假身份获取作弊信息，并运用心理战术揭露和打击作弊者。尽管面临挑战，Riot的努力已见成效，其游戏《Valorant》中作弊行为比例已降至不到1%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏反作弊系统，特别是内核级反作弊技术的使用及其隐私、安全和系统稳定性影响

不同观点：
• 反对内核级反作弊技术：
   - 认为内核级反作弊（如Riot的Vanguard）是对隐私的侵犯，可能被用于收集用户数据，尤其是与中国有关的公司时更加令人担忧（[prkl]）。
   - 这种技术类似于警察在每个人的房子里安装摄像头，本质上是不合适的（[prkl]）。
   - 内核级反作弊技术不稳定，可能导致系统崩溃和蓝屏（[snailmailman]，[OrvalWintermute]）。
   - 用户不愿意为玩游戏而让出系统的底层控制权，尤其是当这种技术可能带来安全隐患时（[shmerl]，[josephcsible]）。

• 支持内核级反作弊技术：
   - 一些玩家和开发者认为内核级反作弊是有效的对抗作弊手段，尤其是在免费游戏中，能够防止大多数作弊行为（[arh68]）。
   - 部分人认为玩家并没有对反作弊系统表现出明显的反感，且这种技术对游戏公平性有帮助（[arh68]）。

• 对反作弊技术的替代方案讨论：
   - 提出可以通过收费账户等方式减少作弊者，而不需要内核级反作弊技术（[oliwarner]）。
   - 未来可能通过Windows的安全功能实现用户级别的反作弊系统，减少内核级干预（[doikor]）。
   - 有人提出游戏流媒体服务可能是一种避免在本地硬件运行反作弊系统的方法（[to-too-two]）。

补充讨论：
• 反作弊技术对系统和多操作系统的干扰：
   - 安全启动（Secure Boot）可能影响双系统用户，尤其是那些使用非主流操作系统（如Haiku）的用户（[smallstepforman]）。
   
• 作弊问题和游戏公司的责任：
   - 有评论指出，一些游戏公司（如Valve）对作弊问题重视不够，可能因为作弊者与皮肤交易者有重叠，成为收入来源（[jokoon]）。

• 对内核级反作弊技术是否为“恶意软件”或“rootkit”的质疑：
   - 有用户直接称这种技术为“rootkit”或“恶意软件风格的访问”（[ziggure]，[shmerl]）。

争议焦点：内核级反作弊技术是否必要，及其对用户隐私和系统安全的潜在影响。

43888501.article_content:
For as long as there have been video games, there have been people willing to find ways to cheat. Hobbyists have long dedicated themselves to finding vulnerabilities in games, often with the goal of developing cheats that they could share or sell. But ever since online competitive gaming became a legitimate profession, that hobby-hacking has morphed into an entire industry that aims to sell an unfair advantage to those willing to pay.
Developing and selling video game cheats
can be a lucrative business
, and video game developers have in recent years had to beef up their anti-cheat teams, whose mission is to ban cheaters, neutralize the software they use, as well as go after cheat developers.
More companies
are taking the
somewhat
controversial
step of deploying anti-cheat systems that run at the
kernel level
, meaning they have the highest privileges in the operating system and can potentially monitor everything that happens on the machine the game is run on.
One of the most prominent kernel-level anti-cheat systems is
Vanguard
, developed by Riot Games, which makes
popular
titles
such as multiplayer online battle arena game
League of Legends and
online first-person shooter
Valorant
.
Essentially, Vanguard “forces cheats to be visible,” said Phillip Koskinas, the director and head of anti-cheat at Riot who
describes
himself
as “an anti-cheat artisan” who was “put on this earth for the one singular purpose of banning cheaters from online video games.”.
Thanks to Vanguard and the anti-cheat team led by Koskinas,  Riot bans thousands of cheaters on
Valorant
every day, according to a chart shared with TechCrunch.
A chart showing the number of cheaters banned per day, and the type of bans, on riot games’ first-person shooter valorant.
Riot’s efforts seem to be working. As of early 2025, the percentage of
Valorant
“ranked” games — meaning competitive matches — that have cheaters is now less than 1% globally,
the company says
.
In an interview with TechCrunch, Koskinas detailed the various strategies that the anti-cheat team at Riot uses to fight cheaters and cheat developers: leveraging the security features in the Windows operating system, fingerprinting cheaters’ hardware to stop them from reoffending, infiltrating cheat communities, and playing psychological games in an effort to discredit cheaters.
‘We can just make them look like fools’
Much of Koskinas and his team’s efforts stem from Vanguard having the deepest level of access to a gamer’s computer. To weed out cheaters, Vanguard takes advantage of some of the security features already built into Windows.
First, Koskinas explained, the anti-cheat software “almost universally” enforces some of Windows’ most important security features, such as
Trusted Platform Module
, a hardware-based security component, and
Secure Boot
. These two technologies check if a computer has been modified or tampered with, such as by malware or a cheat, and prevents it from booting if so. Then, Vanguard checks that all of the computer’s hardware drivers, which allow the operating system to communicate with the hardware, are up to date to identify additional hardware that can enable cheating. Finally, Vanguard prevents cheats from loading and executing code in the kernel’s memory.
“Basically, all the security features that Microsoft and hardware manufacturers have leveraged to protect the operating system, we use or enforce,” Koskinas told TechCrunch. “We have to have a playground where we can play. We have to enforce a certain level of security.”
But fighting cheaters is not just about technology; it’s also about understanding the cheaters themselves and how they operate.
Koskinas’s team has a “reconnaissance arm,” he said, whose primary responsibility is to obtain and catalog threats, which sometimes involves acquiring cheats. The team obtains cheats in part by using sock puppet identities that have infiltrated cheater and cheat developer communities for years, akin to undercover operations.
“We’ve even gone as far as giving anti-cheat information to establish credibility. We’ll masquerade as though it was something we [reverse engineered], and explain how an anti-cheat technique works to demonstrate that we know stuff,” said Koskinas. “And then leverage our way into something in development, and then sit there until it launches, allow it to acquire users and then ban everybody.”
Contact Us
Do you develop cheats, hack video games, or work in anti-cheat? We’d love to hear from you. From a non-work device and network, you can contact Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai securely on Signal at +1 917 257 1382, or via Telegram and Keybase @lorenzofb, or
email
.

43888501.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了视频游戏中的作弊问题以及游戏公司如何打击作弊行为。随着网络竞技的发展，作弊已成为一个利润丰厚的产业，作弊者通过销售不公平的优势获利。为了应对这一问题，游戏开发商加强了反作弊团队，其中Riot Games开发的Vanguard反作弊系统尤为突出。Vanguard在操作系统内核层面运行，能够深入监控玩家的电脑，每天禁言大量作弊者。Riot利用Windows的安全功能，检查硬件驱动程序更新，防止作弊软件加载和执行代码。此外，Riot还通过渗透作弊社区、使用虚假身份获取作弊信息，并运用心理战术揭露和打击作弊者。尽管面临挑战，Riot的努力已见成效，其游戏《Valorant》中作弊行为比例已降至不到1%。
43888501.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏反作弊系统，特别是内核级反作弊技术的使用及其隐私、安全和系统稳定性影响

不同观点：
• 反对内核级反作弊技术：
   - 认为内核级反作弊（如Riot的Vanguard）是对隐私的侵犯，可能被用于收集用户数据，尤其是与中国有关的公司时更加令人担忧（[prkl]）。
   - 这种技术类似于警察在每个人的房子里安装摄像头，本质上是不合适的（[prkl]）。
   - 内核级反作弊技术不稳定，可能导致系统崩溃和蓝屏（[snailmailman]，[OrvalWintermute]）。
   - 用户不愿意为玩游戏而让出系统的底层控制权，尤其是当这种技术可能带来安全隐患时（[shmerl]，[josephcsible]）。

• 支持内核级反作弊技术：
   - 一些玩家和开发者认为内核级反作弊是有效的对抗作弊手段，尤其是在免费游戏中，能够防止大多数作弊行为（[arh68]）。
   - 部分人认为玩家并没有对反作弊系统表现出明显的反感，且这种技术对游戏公平性有帮助（[arh68]）。

• 对反作弊技术的替代方案讨论：
   - 提出可以通过收费账户等方式减少作弊者，而不需要内核级反作弊技术（[oliwarner]）。
   - 未来可能通过Windows的安全功能实现用户级别的反作弊系统，减少内核级干预（[doikor]）。
   - 有人提出游戏流媒体服务可能是一种避免在本地硬件运行反作弊系统的方法（[to-too-two]）。

补充讨论：
• 反作弊技术对系统和多操作系统的干扰：
   - 安全启动（Secure Boot）可能影响双系统用户，尤其是那些使用非主流操作系统（如Haiku）的用户（[smallstepforman]）。
   
• 作弊问题和游戏公司的责任：
   - 有评论指出，一些游戏公司（如Valve）对作弊问题重视不够，可能因为作弊者与皮肤交易者有重叠，成为收入来源（[jokoon]）。

• 对内核级反作弊技术是否为“恶意软件”或“rootkit”的质疑：
   - 有用户直接称这种技术为“rootkit”或“恶意软件风格的访问”（[ziggure]，[shmerl]）。

争议焦点：内核级反作弊技术是否必要，及其对用户隐私和系统安全的潜在影响。

data.title: Why Flatpak apps use so much disk space on Linux
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux 包管理工具（如 Flatpak、Snap）的优缺点，尤其是在存储空间、时间和资源消耗方面的影响。

不同观点：
• [loloquwowndueo] 认为包管理工具（特别是 Snap）不尊重用户的计算机资源，导致系统和人的时间成本增加，尤其是在更新时会严重拖慢系统。
• [INTPenis] 表示 Flatpak 在其日常使用中影响不大，虽然占用一定空间，但因为使用不多，所以可以接受，特别是其容器化的优点。
• [qbane] 关注 Flatpak 存储空间无限制增长的问题，引用多个社区和问题报告来说明该问题的普遍性。
• [massysett] 以幽默的方式指出 Flatpak 与 IKEA 平包的对比，指出 Flatpak 实际上增加了空间占用，而不是减少。
• [mcv] 建议允许不同版本的库共存，而不是打包所有依赖，以减少空间占用，类似于 npm 的做法。
• [jasonpeacock] 对 Flatpak 不适合服务器使用的观点提出疑问，想知道具体是哪些桌面特性导致这一问题。
• [Havoc] 以讽刺的方式表达对“在我的电脑上能运行，我们就发布我的电脑”这种做法的不满。
• [account-5] 比较了 Windows 的便携式应用程序和 Linux 的 Flatpak，质疑为什么 Linux 的解决方案会如此不同。
• [_Soulou] 关注 Flatpak 的内存使用问题，认为多次加载相同库的不同版本会增加内存消耗。
• [butz] 提出通过选择相同运行时版本来减少 Flatpak 的磁盘空间占用，并讨论了运行时版本过渡期间可能导致的多版本问题。
• [wltr] 对原文内容的低质量表示不满，认为评论比文章本身更有价值。
• [haunter] 质疑 Flatpak 比 Appimage 更流行的原因，认为 Appimage 更便携。
• [ReptileMan] 批评不断尝试重新发明静态链接器，认为这是在重复 Windows 的 DLL 地狱问题。
• [gjsman-1000] 对比了 Linux 桌面和任天堂的 Horizon 操作系统，认为现代操作系统设计应该更简洁和高效。

• 对如何有效管理库版本和减少空间占用提出了多种建议和比较，包括与 Windows 的 npm 等工具的对比。
• 对 Flatpak 和 Appimage 的流行程度和优劣也有一定的讨论和不同看法。
• 部分用户对现代 Linux 桌面环境的复杂性和效率提出了批评和反思。

data.title: Helmdar: 3D Scanning Brooklyn on Rollerblades
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者喜欢深夜穿轮滑探索城市，特别是在波士顿和纽约。在夜间，城市街道变得空旷，垃圾车、维修工人等开始工作，使城市为新一天做好准备。作者通过轮滑以不同速度感受城市的细节与整体。作者还介绍了一个名为"Stickdar"的实验项目，利用2D LiDAR扫描仪记录城市环境，并将其可视化。后来，作者尝试将LiDAR安装在头盔上，结合手机的6自由度追踪功能，构建了一个名为"Helmdar"的系统，通过手机和LiDAR的结合，实时绘制出周围环境的3D点云地图。这一项目被视为一种"奇特相机"，通过不完全精确的成像系统进行创意表达。作者详细描述了硬件和软件的实现方式，并通过照片展示了实际效果。

43889875.article_content:
One of my favorite joys is exploring a city late at night on rollerblades. I’ve been doing it fairly regularly for about
10 years now, first in Boston and then in NYC. Every time day turns to night and back again a city takes a breath. At
night people flow out or huddle up in buildings, leaving the streets clear for the people and machines that reset
the urban environment for the next day. Garbage trucks lumber about, workers unload fresh stock at stores, repairs
happen in subway tunnels and on roads. Without all the people it’s easier to see the naked form of the streets,
buildings, and infrastructure.
When you’re moving slow you spend more time taking in the details. When you’re moving fast the world becomes a blur. The
world around you is a brush that paints into your perception, and the speed of the brush strokes helps set the style of
the painting. I like rollerblading in particular because it gives those perceptual brush strokes a lot of range. You can
quickly stop and soak in a detail, change direction, occupy a tight space, or fly downhill in a long straight line.
Stickdar
Some years ago I picked up a 2D LiDAR scanner (RPLidar A1) without a particular purpose in mind. As it spins it tells
you its current angle and the distance to the environment in the direction it’s pointing. They’re often used in robot
vacuums to map walls and other obstacles. One night in 2021 I put it on the end of a stick and carried it around with my
laptop recording timestamped measurements from it. By putting each scan sweep on its own layer I could make
visualizations like this:
Taken outside my apartment at the time during heavy snowfall. You can see the path cut through the snow on the
sidewalk, the apartment building wall, windows, cars along the sidewalk, and points on a tree.
Walking along the perimeter wall outside New Lab. Just behind the character is scaffolding. There are rectangles from
windows. And if I remember right there was snow on the ground at that time too. This one is much more distorted because
I wasn’t so careful to keep the sensor stable while moving.
I think about devices like this as “weird cameras” - imperfect leaky imaging systems that don’t faithfully reproduce
a precise representation of what they are pointed at. Instead they mix in side channels that the user or environment can
affect, and that frees them up for more interesting creative expression.
Helmdar
While I was experimenting with the stickdar I had the idea that it would be fun to make maps on a larger scale by
carrying it around while I was rollerblading. But when I tried that out the maps were very chaotic because it was harder
to keep it steady. I moved onto other projects, but then the other week this project thread popped back into mind.
Over the years I’ve done various projects which needed 6 DoF tracking through space (i.e. machine needs to know where it
is and where it is pointing). A very convenient way to achieve this nowadays for something quick and dirty is to use
mobile phones, because they come with AR frameworks that know how to use the sensors and cameras onboard to do very good
“inside-out” (no external sensors) 6 DoF tracking. On Android that’s even exposed to web browsers via the WebXR API so
you can bash together a web app to access that data, no app development required (hot tip: works on the Quest VR
headsets too, including hand tracking, which I’ve
had fun using for projects in the past
).
So when the stickdar popped back into mind I started thinking about attaching the LiDAR to a phone to track its position
and orientation in space. Then I could work out the position of all the points returned by the sensor in 3D world space,
building up a point cloud map of the world as I moved through it. In general doing this is a problem known as
simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)
, and
nowadays there are plenty of very good ways to solve it. But in the spirit of weird cameras, because I was curious about
how well this would work, and for fun I decided to try it this way.
Here’s what I came up with:
I built a frame out of aluminum extrusion and attached the phone (a Pixel 6) and the LiDAR to the front with some laser
cut and 3D printed brackets. I affixed this to the helmet using flexible brackets printed in TPU and VHB double-stick
tape, with some white duct tape for insurance. The LiDAR plugs into the phone’s USB-C jack via a USB-to-serial adapter
for data and power. The squares on the side are AprilTags, which are visual tracking markers that I wanted to try using
for tracking the helmet in space to do some VFX experiments. They’re unrelated to the mapping. The whole thing felt
surprisingly sturdy but was pretty front-heavy so I added a power bank on the back purely as a counterweight.
(Photo credit: Sally)
On the software side, I wrote an Android app that implements a driver for the LiDAR. This wasn’t a big challenge because
of this nice
usb-serial-for-android
library and
an existing python library

data.title: Graceful Shutdown in Go: Practical Patterns
data.author: mkl95
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Go应用中的优雅关闭模式，主要包括三个核心步骤：关闭请求入口、等待正在处理的请求完成、释放关键资源。优雅关闭首先需要捕获操作系统信号（如SIGTERM、SIGINT、SIGHUP），Go运行时默认处理这些信号，但可以通过`os/signal`包注册自定义信号处理函数来实现优雅关闭。使用带缓冲的通道（容量为1）可以确保信号不会丢失，Go会在收到指定信号时将其发送到通道，开发者可以手动处理这些信号并执行自定义的关闭逻辑。通过这种方式，应用可以在接收到终止信号时从容地完成资源释放和清理工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kubernetes环境下的优雅关闭（graceful shutdown）和相关技术挑战

不同观点：
• **zdc1** 认为Kubernetes中负载均衡器更新目标IP所需时间较长，导致在pod终止前需要花大量时间确保流量被排空。他通过添加preStop hook和15秒的sleep显著改善了HTTP 503错误率。这为应用程序简化了处理SIGTERM的逻辑。

on

Graceful Shutdown in Go: Practical Patterns
Graceful shutdown in any application generally satisfies three minimum conditions:
Close the entry point by stopping new requests or messages from sources like HTTP, pub/sub systems, etc. However, keep outgoing connections to third-party services like databases or caches active.
Wait for all ongoing requests to finish. If a request takes too long, respond with a graceful error.
Release critical resources such as database connections, file locks, or network listeners. Do any final cleanup.
This article focuses on HTTP servers and containerized applications, but the core ideas apply to all types of applications.
1. Catching the Signal
#
Before we handle graceful shutdown, we first need to catch termination signals. These signals tell our application it’s time to exit and begin the shutdown process.
So, what are signals?
In Unix-like systems, signals are software interrupts. They notify a process that something has happened and it should take action. When a signal is sent, the operating system interrupts the normal flow of the process to deliver the notification.
Here are a few possible behaviors:
Signal handler
: A process can register a handler (a function) for a specific signal. This function runs when that signal is received.
Default action
: If no handler is registered, the process follows the default behavior for that signal. This might mean terminating, stopping, continuing, or ignoring the process.
Unblockable signals
: Some signals, like
SIGKILL
(signal number 9), cannot be caught or ignored. They may terminate the process.
When your Go application starts, even before your
main
function runs, the Go runtime automatically registers signal handlers for many signals (
SIGTERM
,
SIGQUIT
,
SIGILL
,
SIGTRAP
, and others). However, for graceful shutdown, only three termination signals are typically important:
SIGTERM
(Termination): A standard and polite way to ask a process to terminate. It does not force the process to stop. Kubernetes sends this signal when it wants your application to exit before it forcibly kills it.
SIGINT
(Interrupt): Sent when the user wants to stop a process from the terminal, usually by pressing
Ctrl+C
.
SIGHUP
(Hang up): Originally used when a terminal disconnected. Now, it is often repurposed to signal an application to reload its configuration.
People mostly care about
SIGTERM
and
SIGINT
.
SIGHUP
is less used today for shutdown and more for reloading configs. You can find more about this in
SIGHUP Signal for Configuration Reloads
.
By default, when your application receives a
SIGTERM
,
SIGINT
, or
SIGHUP
, the Go runtime will terminate the application.
Insight: How Go Terminates Your Application
When your Go app gets a
SIGTERM
, the runtime first catches it using a built-in handler. It checks if a custom handler is registered. If not, the runtime disables its own handler temporarily, and sends the same signal (
SIGTERM
) to the application again. This time, the OS handles it using the default behavior, which is to terminate the process.
You can override this by registering your own signal handler using the
os/signal
package.
func
main
()
{
signalChan
:=
make
(
chan
os
.
Signal
,
1
)
signal
.
Notify
(
signalChan
,
syscall
.
SIGINT
,
syscall
.
SIGTERM
)
// Setup work here
<-
signalChan
fmt
.
Println
(
"Received termination signal, shutting down..."
)
}
Graceful shutdown begins with signal setup
signal.Notify
tells the Go runtime to deliver specified signals to a channel instead of using the default behavior. This allows you to handle them manually and prevents the application from terminating automatically.
A buffered channel with a capacity of 1 is a good choice for reliable signal handling. Internally, Go sends signals to this channel using a
select
statement with a default case:
select
{
case
c
<-
sig
:
default
:
}
This is different from the usual
select
used with receiving channels. When used for sending:
If the buffer has space, the signal is sent and the code continues.
If the buffer is full, the signal is discarded, and the
default
case runs. If you’re using an unbuffered channel and no goroutine is actively receiving, the signal will be missed.
Even though it can only hold one signal, this buffered channel helps avoid missing that first signal while your app is still initializing and not yet listening.
You can call
Notify
multiple times for the same signal. Go will send that signal to all registered channels.
When you press
Ctrl+C
more than once, it doesn’t automatically kill the app. The first
Ctrl+C
sends a
SIGINT
to the foreground process. Pressing it again usually sends another
SIGINT
, not
SIGKILL
. Most terminals, like bash or other Linux shells, do not escalate the signal automatically. If you want to force a stop, you must send
SIGKILL
manually using
kill -9
.

data.article_summary: ThunderScope是一款全新类型的示波器，具备高速、灵活和完全开放的特点，目前已开放预订。项目更新报告提到，团队正在全力推进Rev. 5的PCB设计，特别注重将ADC、时钟生成器、FPGA及其电源供应全部安装在散热片下，并增加了弹簧夹使散热片兼具屏蔽功能。设计中对四个前端做了细微差别处理，以测试接地和切口对衰减器电路的影响，并通过脚本改进了KiCad的长度匹配功能以实现延迟匹配。由于新设计和个人原因，产品将延期交付。接下来的步骤包括手动构建和测试Rev. 5，组装开发版PCB，制作测试夹具，并预计在9月前完成发货。项目进展将通过GitHub Issues公开跟踪。

43852217.article_content:
ThunderScope
A new type of oscilloscope that’s fast, flexible, and completely open
Available for pre-order
View Purchasing Options
Apr 30, 2025
Project update
11 of 11
Revving Up for Production
by
Aleksa B
Hi all,
I’ve spent the last month-and-a-half heads down on the PCB layout for Rev. 5…
I didn’t expect it to take that long, but then again this is the most effort I’ve ever put into a PCB design - it just had to be perfect!
High effort silkscreen aside, I’m especially proud of fitting the ADC, Clock Generator, FPGA and all their power supplies under the heatsink. I added spring clips so the heatsink can function as a shield for the whole acquisition section as well. Here’s some work-in-progress pictures from when I first placed everything (left) and at some point into the layout (right).
I also made the four front ends ever so slightly different from one another to test how the cutouts and grounding affect the elusive attenuator circuit. CH1 has a solid pour to all the components, while the other channels do not. CH3 and CH4 have progressively fewer ground plane cutouts than CH2. I’ve also via stitched the front end as I think that may have caused the wobbliness in the frequency response as dropping down a few layers causes the ground reference to change and, without vias nearby, the return current will have a hard time making it there.
The other change in the front end is the (re)addition of a trim cap (C1059). Since the buffer’s capacitance can vary from part to part, we want to trim it to a known level. This capacitance is about 2.4 pF, while variation in it will be sub 1 pF. This wasn’t much compared to the >100pF lower leg of the attenuator in previous designs, but with this new improved design we need to worry about it again. Trade-offs, trade-offs everywhere!
Teaching KiCad a New Trick - Matching Delays
At time of writing, KiCad only understands the length of traces and pins. When length matching, it takes length as a single number added up across every layer. This leads to delay mismatches, as the signals on the inner layers are slower than the signals on the outer layers. When assigning pin lengths, you need to arbitrarily choose a layer to convert a delay value (given by the manufacturer), to a length. This also results in delay mismatches.
I wanted to do this right, just like Altium does, but I didn’t want to have to calculate and add up all the delay values by hand in a spreadsheet. So I made a script to rewrite custom design rules to try to get KiCad’s length matching to be delay matching (including pad delays).
It was only slightly off from KiCad’s reported lengths, so not bad, as we just need consistency from trace to trace, not absolute accuracy. But then, as soon as I added a curved tuning pattern, it all fell apart.
I found out it was miscounting certain segments because of a small math error (normalizing the angle to [0,2*pi] when it should be [0,pi]) and got it working again! Below is the output of the script when tuning the skews on the PCIe lanes.
The rewriting design rules bit doesn’t work all that well given the slight discrepancy with the KiCad reported lengths and the whole delay-to-length conversion just assuming top layer for everything. However, if you just look at the delay deltas, then it’s pretty usable for tuning! In fact, I did all the delay matching on TS with this tool. If you want to try it yourself, I’ve put the script up in its
own separate repo
.
Next Steps, Accountability, and New Shipping Estimates
Now to address the elephant in the room, we won’t be shipping on time. The new interposer design, the switch to KiCad, and some personal issues all contributed to this. I take full responsibility and am committed to getting this done as quickly as possible while still holding myself and the project to the highest standards. So first things first, what are the next steps?
Hand Build Rev. 5:
Boards arrive at the end of April and I expect to get them built within a day or two of receiving them.
Test Rev. 5:
This should take no longer than two weeks.
Once these are done, I can roll any minor changes into a Rev 5.1. If there are any major changes needed, however unlikely, I will repeat the above process with a new rev.
Next up,
Get Dev. Edition PCBs Assembled:
send the design to a CM and wait a month or so.
Build Test Fixtures and Assembly Jigs:
use the time the CM is working on the PCBAs.
Test and Ship Dev. Edition units:
these should reach backers in July.
A month after shipping Dev. Edition units (to give time for any last bugs to be reported), we’ll do the same process as above for the rest of the units. We can improve our fixtures and jigs while the boards are out for fab and assembly, and then we should be able to ship in September.
To keep myself accountable, I will be using
GitHub Issues
to publicly track the tasks left before shipping, so check those out if you’re ever wondering how things are going between updates. Or, you can ask me directly through the project qu

data.title: Show HN: Driverless print server for legacy printers, profit goes to open-source
data.author: ValdikSS
data.article_summary: UoWPrint是一个现代打印服务器，旨在为旧款打印机、扫描仪和多功能一体机添加无线功能。它作为易于使用的附加设备，可以将旧的USB打印机转换为Wi-Fi设备，无需安装特定驱动程序即可从Windows、macOS、Linux、iOS和Android设备进行打印和扫描。UoWPrint自带通用驱动程序，运行在服务器上，从而免去在电脑上安装驱动的麻烦。它支持多种品牌和型号的设备，如HP、Samsung、Xerox、Canon等，并兼容多种操作系统。该项目的动机是减少电子废物，提升便利性，并重新利用单板计算机。UoWPrint无需互联网连接，仅用于时间同步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过技术手段解决旧设备兼容性及网络打印和扫描问题，同时涉及开源项目和安全性讨论。

不同观点：
• [raffraffraff] 认为现代高性价比的扫描仪质量不佳，尤其是对艺术家而言选择有限。通过使用Raspberry Pi和定制软件，成功让旧设备重新发挥作用，并享受了项目带来的乐趣。
• [braincode] 提出是否存在一种“物理虚拟打印机”，可以欺骗操作系统认为它是真实打印机，并能在“打印”后生成PDF文件存储在设备上。
• [veggieroll] 支持使用Raspberry Pi进行网络打印和扫描，强调了避免厂商软件不安全性的好处，并表示该方案在功能上不逊色于厂商打印机。
• [1970-01-01] 认为该项目有潜力成为像Dropbox一样的热门服务，特别是在处理不兼容现代设备的旧打印机方面。
• [kevinsync] 仅对项目使用的域名美学做出评论，未深入讨论技术内容。
• [fnwbr] 关注在多设备环境下如何配置SSID和密码，以确保打印安全性。
• [Beijinger] 对设备绑定单一打印机表示不满，认为应支持更多设备。
• [jessekv] 分享了自己使用Airport Express解决类似问题的经验。

data.title: pdfCropMargins – auto-detect and cut PDF margins for small-screen reading
data.author: aragonite
data.article_summary: **pdfCropMargins** 是一个命令行工具，用于自动裁剪PDF文件的页边距，以提升阅读体验。它具有多种功能，包括自动检测并裁剪指定百分比的边距、统一页面尺寸、支持Linux/Windows/OS X等多种系统，以及可选的图形用户界面（GUI）用于交互式裁剪。它还能够处理扫描噪声较大的PDF文件，支持对加密文件的简单处理，并提供撤销功能。用户可以通过pip安装该工具，基本功能开箱即用，部分高级功能需要依赖pdftoppm或Ghostscript。最新版本增加了更多自定义选项和对单个页边距的裁剪支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同的工具和方法用于文档处理（尤其是PDF优化或裁剪）

不同观点：
• [throwaway81523] 认为CUPS已经提供了实现该功能的途径，暗示可能不需要其他额外工具。
  
• [gumboshoes] 提出Briss和其他一些分支工具（如Briss的forks）也具备类似的PDF处理功能，并提供了一个链接（https://briss.sourceforge.net/）作为参考。他还提到自己使用的工具效果很好，但记不清具体是哪一个。

• [hyperpl] 推荐使用k2pdfopt的命令行界面（CLI），认为它对于各种屏幕阅读设备的支持非常全面，并提供了工具的链接（https://www.willus.com/k2pdfopt/）。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多个具体工具：CUPS、Briss及其forks、k2pdfopt。这些工具各有不同的功能侧重和使用场景。
  
• [gumboshoes] 强调了一些工具的分支版本（forks）可能在功能上有所改进或变化，但没有具体说明是哪些forks。

• [hyperpl] 特别指出了k2pdfopt的命令行界面以及其在处理不同屏幕阅读设备方面的优势，表明该工具在特定需求下（如屏幕阅读优化）可能更为合适。

争议焦点：目前讨论中并没有明显的争议，更多的是不同用户推荐各自常用的工具，并提供相关链接供参考。主要的差异体现在对不同工具的功能和适用场景的看法上。
